settings.apiKeyDisclaimer: API keys are stored exclusively encrypted, locally on this computer (in the Electron main process, via safeStorage) and never leave that process — not even towards this interface.
settings.modelIdTitle: Model ID (adjust if there are errors)
settings.allowFallback: With "Automatic": fall back to the paid API if no local agent is available
settings.localAgentsIntro: Installation and sign-in can be triggered directly below - this opens a terminal window with the provider's official command; you finish the rest (installation or browser login) there yourself. The detected status here updates automatically once the CLI is available and signed in.
settings.installLoginHint: Terminal opened - the status here updates automatically once you switch back after finishing there.
settings.workspaceIntro: A shared folder for new projects. Set up here once as a Git repository; every new project then creates its own subfolder inside it without being rejected as "inside another Git project". Existing, separate Git projects elsewhere are unaffected.
settings.languageIntro: Changes the language of the entire interface immediately.

councilUsage.intro: A participant call can include several internal model calls. Only reported token values and costs are shown; no remaining subscription quota can be inferred from this.

companyTruth.intro: Fixed facts and rules about your company (product, tech, marketing, legal, decisions) – independent of any single conversation. Optionally included in Compare/Team/Council, so every provider starts from the same facts instead of contradicting each other.
companyTruth.factPlaceholder: e.g. §34a Sachkunde PRO has no native iOS app.
companyTruth.noEntries: No entries yet – add the first fact above.

usageHistory.heading: Usage history
usageHistory.intro1: The last up to 200 runs. Participant and agent calls can include several internal model calls. Missing measurements are unknown; reported costs make no statement about subscription charges or remaining quota.
usageHistory.intro2: New Council and Coding measurements are stored from this version onward. Older task measurements appear where already available.

help.overviewHeading: Overview: what does each tab do?
help.tabParallelDesc: shows several answers to the same question side by side.
help.tabTeamDesc: several providers share one task, one combined result.
help.tabCouncilDesc: multi-stage discussion (independent answers, critique, synthesis) for a well-considered decision.
help.tabCodingDesc: a single agent works directly in a folder you choose.
help.tabWorkflowDesc: the big pipeline for real projects: specification → council → task graph → execution → release. See below for details.
help.tabSettingsDesc: API keys, local agents, backend choice, workshop folder.
help.providerSetupHeading: Setting up a provider - API or local
help.providerSetupIntro1: In settings, you choose between three options per provider:
help.providerSetupIntro2: (your own API key, cost per use),
help.providerSetupIntro3: (the locally installed CLI agent, usually already included in a subscription) or
help.providerSetupIntro4: (uses the local agent if available; only falls back to the paid API if you have explicitly allowed that via the checkbox).
help.apiKeyTestIntro: There is no format check for an API key - just paste it in and click
help.apiKeyTestOutro: , that is the only real verification.
help.localAgentAuthIntro: For local agents, the app shows the detected sign-in status. For Claude Code and Grok Build this is a real check (signed in yes/no). For Codex and Antigravity, the sign-in status always shows
help.localAgentAuthOutro: once the CLI is found - that is normal and not an error: as of now, neither CLI offers a way to query the sign-in status without a real run.
help.workflowIntro: Before anything runs, a specification must be approved. A task graph created by the council breaks the goal down into individual tasks. Each task runs in its own isolated workspace (its own Git worktree) - implementer and reviewer (optionally also a challenger) check independently before anything is integrated into the project.
help.statusRunningDesc: the task is currently being worked on.
help.statusAwaitingPermissionDesc: the agent is asking for extended access (e.g. shell commands). This is normal, not a disruption - confirm once and it continues.
help.statusAwaitingInstallDesc: a required tool is missing; the app suggests an install command that you can review and confirm.
help.statusReviewDesc: checks and reviews passed successfully, awaiting your approval.
help.statusPausedDesc: e.g. because an agent's session limit was reached. Nothing is lost - can be resumed later at the same point.
help.statusFailedDesc: checks or review did not pass; a new attempt can be started.
help.statusEscalatedDesc: a real decision from you is needed (e.g. a change to the allowed scope) before it can continue.
help.budgetsInfo: Each task also has a correction and time budget (how many correction rounds, and how long it may run actively) - if a task needs more, the budget can be specifically adjusted.
help.gitQuestionTitle: Does my project folder already need a Git repository?
help.gitAnswerPart1: No, the Workflow tab handles that automatically - the same applies to all three agents, it is not a Codex-specific quirk. An empty folder is initialized automatically the first time. An existing folder with Git history is simply reused. An existing folder
help.gitNoCommitBold: with files but no prior Git commit
help.gitAnswerPart2: (e.g. an existing project that was never in Git) is rejected instead - there, you must once run
help.gitAnswerPart3: and make a first commit by hand before selecting the folder here. The Coding tab, by contrast, needs no Git at all.
help.usageIntro1: The Usage tab shows what this app itself has measured: calls and duration per run. This is
help.usageIntro2: the exact remaining quota of a subscription - there is no reliable source for that; the app only shows its own, actually measured usage.
help.faq1Question: I just installed a CLI, but the app still shows "{{status}}".
help.faq1Answer: Reopen settings once, or restart the app - otherwise the system path (PATH) is not re-read.
help.faq2Answer: A task may only change the files/folders listed there - this protects the rest of the project from unwanted changes.
help.versionUpdatesInfo: New versions are checked automatically at startup and, if available, downloaded in the background - you are always asked before installation.
help.supportIntro: Question or problem? Write to me directly.

onboarding.welcomeIntro: Set up at least one provider here to get started: either with your own API key, or via one of the supported AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok Build) - installation and sign-in can be triggered directly below, which opens a terminal window you finish yourself. Everything here can be changed later in Settings at any time.
